query: What was the position of Jean Baptiste Androuet du Cerceau under the man who was King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from 1573 to 1575?

Jean Baptiste André de Cerceau, also known as Jean Baptiste de Cerceau, was a French nobleman and politician who played a significant role in the history of Poland and Lithuania. He served as the King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from 1573 to 1673 and as the King of France from 1648 until his death in 1673.

Cerceau was born on September 29, 1590, in the village of Cernyka, Poland. He studied under the tutelage of the Polish-Lithuanian Academy of Sciences and later became a member of the Polish nobility. After studying law at the University of Kraków, he moved to France where he worked as a lawyer and politician.

Cerceau was appointed as the King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth in 1573 by King Sigismund III (1568–1594) and later became the King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania in 1572, 1573, and 1575. He played a significant role in the history of Poland and Lithuania during his reign, as he was involved in several conflicts with neighboring powers such as the Habsburgs and the Habsburg-Rheinland-Pfalz.

Cerceau's position under King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from 1573 to 1673 is considered a significant milestone in the history of Poland, as it marked the beginning of religious tolerance for nobility and free persons within the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. He also played a crucial role in the conflicts between the pro-Habsburg and pro-French political factions during his reign.
retrieved_context: Henry III of France: Henry III (19 September 1551 – 2 August 1589; born "Alexandre Édouard de France", Polish: "Henryk Walezy" , Lithuanian: "Henrikas Valua" ) was King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from 1573 to 1575 and King of France from 1574 until his death.  He was the last French monarch of the House of Valois.

Warsaw Confederation: The Warsaw Confederation, signed on January 28, 1573 by the Polish national assembly ("sejm konwokacyjny") in Warsaw, was the first European act granting religious freedoms.  It was an important development in the history of Poland and Lithuania that extended religious tolerance to nobility and free persons within the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and is considered the formal beginning of religious freedom in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.  While it did not prevent all conflict based on religion, it did make the Commonwealth a much safer and more tolerant place than most of contemporaneous Europe, especially during the subsequent Thirty Years' War.

Michał Korybut Wiśniowiecki: Michael I (Polish: "Michał Korybut Wiśniowiecki" , Lithuanian: "Mykolas I Kaributas Višnioveckis" ; May 31, 1640 – November 10, 1673) was the ruler of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth as King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania from September 29, 1669 until his death in 1673.  Michael's reign was marked by struggles between the pro-Habsburg and pro-French political factions.
